subject: Environment
topic: Glaciers of the Himalayas — mixed tiers
description: Major Indian glaciers, sources of rivers, climate-change retreat, GLOF, third pole

questions.stem: The Himalayan glaciated region is sometimes called the:

options.option_text: Third Pole — because of the largest store of frozen freshwater outside the polar regions

questions.explanation: Third Pole — the Hindu Kush-Himalaya (HKH) region, containing the largest mass of glaciers + permafrost outside the Arctic + Antarctic. ~50,000 glaciers spread across 8 countries (Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, Myanmar, Bangladesh). Source of 10 major Asian rivers — Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra, Yangtze, Yellow, Mekong, Salween, Irrawaddy, Tarim, Amu Darya — supporting ~2 billion people. ICIMOD (International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development, HQ Kathmandu) — coordinates HKH research. Glaciers are retreating ~10-30 m/year on average, with high variability. NASA / ISRO observations confirm consistent mass loss since the 1970s.

questions.stem: The Gangotri Glacier — source of the Bhagirathi (a head-stream of the Ganga) — is located in:
questions.explanation: Gangotri Glacier — Uttarakhand, Uttarkashi district. ~30 km long, ~2-4 km wide; one of the largest glaciers in the Himalayas. The snout is called GAUMUKH ('cow's mouth') — pilgrim site, source of the Bhagirathi. Bhagirathi joins the Alaknanda at Devprayag → Ganga. Glacier is retreating ~22 m/year (recent decades). Other major glaciers in Uttarakhand: Pindari (Pindar, an Alaknanda tributary), Milam (largest in Kumaon), Khatling (Bhilangana, a Bhagirathi trib). Yamunotri Glacier — source of Yamuna, also Uttarakhand.

questions.stem: The Siachen Glacier, the world's HIGHEST and one of the longest non-polar glaciers, is in:

options.option_text: Eastern Karakoram (Ladakh) — under Indian control since Operation Meghdoot, 1984

questions.explanation: Siachen Glacier — Eastern Karakoram, Ladakh, India. ~76 km long, world's longest non-polar mountain glaciers. Highest battlefield in the world — Indian and Pakistani troops face off at altitudes up to ~6,700 m. India captured the glacier in OPERATION MEGHDOOT (13 Apr 1984), under Lt Gen P.N. Hoon. Siachen Base Camp ~3,650 m; outposts up to ~6,700 m. Climate hazards (avalanche, frostbite) cause more casualties than combat. The glacier is a source of the Nubra river → Shyok → Indus. Recent ecological concern — glacier is retreating rapidly; military activities accelerate melt due to disposed waste, fuel.

questions.stem: GLOF — a major Himalayan hazard — stands for:

options.option_text: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood — sudden release of water from a glacier-dammed or moraine-dammed lake

questions.explanation: GLOF — Glacial Lake Outburst Flood. Climate-warming melts glaciers → meltwater accumulates behind moraine (debris) dams; the dam fails → catastrophic downstream flood. Examples affecting India: KEDARNATH FLOODS, June 2013 — Chorabari Glacier moraine breach + cloudburst → ~6,000 deaths in Uttarakhand. South Lhonak Lake GLOF, Sikkim, October 2023 — wiped out the Teesta-III hydropower dam at Chungthang and ~50+ villages downstream; ~100 deaths. SIKKIM, NEPAL, BHUTAN — many vulnerable lakes (Imja Tsho, Tsho Rolpa, Lemthang Tsho). NDMA + ICIMOD + ISRO are mapping high-risk lakes. Mitigation: controlled siphoning of lake water (Imja, Nepal — pilot project completed 2016).

questions.stem: The Pindari Glacier is in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Pindari Glacier — Bageshwar district, Kumaon Himalaya, Uttarakhand. ~3 km long, source of the Pindar river (a tributary of the Alaknanda). Famous trek route — Pindari Glacier trek (one of the most accessible glacier treks in India). Other notable Kumaon glaciers: Milam, Kafni, Sunderdhunga. Sikkim — Zemu Glacier (largest in the Eastern Himalayas, source of Teesta). Himachal Pradesh — Bara Shigri (largest in HP, in Lahaul); Chandra; Bhaga; Chhota Shigri (most studied, near Manali). Arunachal Pradesh — small glaciers near Bumla, Sela passes; far less studied.

questions.stem: According to the IPCC and recent ICIMOD reports, Himalayan glaciers are projected to lose what fraction of their mass by 2100 (under high-emission scenarios)?

options.option_text: Up to 80% (for the eastern Himalayas under SSP5-8.5; ~50% even under low-emission scenarios)

questions.explanation: ICIMOD's 'Hindu Kush Himalaya Assessment Report 2019' and the 'Water, Ice, Society and Ecosystems' report 2023: under SSP5-8.5 (high-emission scenario), HKH glaciers could lose up to ~75-80% of their volume by 2100. Even at +1.5 °C (Paris Agreement target), losses ~36%. Eastern Himalayas (Bhutan, Nepal east) most vulnerable; Karakoram has shown some 'Karakoram anomaly' (slight stability or even mass gain) but is now also retreating. Implications: short-term flooding risk (GLOFs, peak flow), long-term DECLINE in dry-season river flow (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra basin water security). Aerosols + black-carbon deposition from Indo-Gangetic Plain pollution accelerates glacier melt.

questions.stem: Which institute / organisation, based at Dehradun, is the nodal body for glaciological research in India?

options.option_text: Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG, Dehradun)

questions.explanation: Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG), Dehradun — autonomous institute under DST, Govt of India. Specialises in Himalayan geology, glaciology, geodynamics, seismology, palaeoclimate. Named after Darashaw Wadia (1883-1969), pioneer Indian geologist. Maintains long-term mass-balance + retreat monitoring of glaciers like Chhota Shigri (Himachal), Dokriani (Uttarakhand). NCPOR (National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research, Goa) — coordinates Antarctic + Arctic research, also Himalayan high-altitude expeditions. ISRO contributes via remote-sensing inventory (Glacial Inventory Atlas of Indian Himalayas).
